name: Plantoir
headline: Plan the plot. Plant your notes. Grow a class website.
tagline: Turns a folder of Markdown notes into a fast, searchable class website.
downloads_note: The download cards on the home page. A card with no 'pinned' version links GitHub's evergreen releases/latest/download/<asset>, which 404s for a platform whose installer is missing from the newest release; such a card is pinned to the last release that has it, and says so. Windows was pinned to 1.1.0 from v1.2.0, which carried the macOS DMG only, until its installer joined v1.4.2 (2026-10-03), and to 1.4.2 for the mac-first v1.4.3 cut until PlantoirSetup.exe joined v1.4.3 (2026-10-07), and to 1.4.3 for the mac-first v1.4.4 cut until PlantoirSetup.exe joined v1.4.4 (2026-10-08): pin it again in any release that lacks PlantoirSetup.exe, and unpin it in the release that ships the Windows installer again. The Mac card was pinned to 1.4.4 from the Windows-only v1.4.5 cut until Plantoir-macOS.dmg joined v1.4.5 (2026-10-08). Windows is pinned to 1.4.5 for the mac-only v1.5.0 cut (2026-10-09), and stays pinned there for the mac-only v1.6.0 and v1.7.0 cuts (2026-10-09): unpin it in the release that ships the Windows installer again. Asset names are frozen (RELEASING.md).

availability.note: On the Mac. The Windows version gets this in a later release.
availability.why: A section describing something the Windows download does not have carries {{availability:<key>}}, which prints the note while 'windows' is false and nothing once it is true. Flip the boolean in the release whose Windows installer has the feature.

redirects.why: Pages that moved, so their old addresses keep working. build.py writes each move into site/_redirects as a permanent (301) redirect, old address and everything under it, and --check refuses a move whose new page is missing, whose old page still exists, or whose old address a page still links to. 'publishing' became 'deploying' in v1.4.4 (#443): DEPLOY puts a site online, PUBLISH only marks a page. Never remove a move: outside links to the old address cannot be counted.

shortcuts.why: Short addresses that land on a section of a page, for saying aloud or printing: build.py writes site/<from>/index.html, a page that sends the browser on to <to> (which may name a #section). Not a _redirects rule, because a redirect to an address with a #section is the one shape whose handling on Netlify was not measured. --check refuses a shortcut whose page or section is missing, or whose address is also a page. /math was promised for the mathematics section in #486 (v1.7.0).
